chosen_property.label: isPartOfEvent
chosen_property.definition: A part-whole relation indicating that an event is a component of a larger event.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links Event to Event for 'part_of'.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: partOfInvoice
candidates.comment: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by. Examples: An online purchase order is part of an invoice. A service request order is part of an invoice. Multiple orders can be part of a single invoice.

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

relations.definition: A semantic connection between a claim and its subject matter
relations.embedding_query_text: about: A semantic connection between a claim and its subject matter

instances: Jonathan Raymond warns of inflationary pressures from energy prices -> Brent crude prices reach $100 since May 2026
Paul Dales predicts UK interest rates will remain at 3.75% -> Brent crude prices reach $100 since May 2026
Kevin Warsh states Fed has "no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation" -> Brent crude prices reach $100 since May 2026

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The 'about' property directly links the claim to its subject matter as defined.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

UK petrol prices -> £1.56
UK diesel prices -> £1.72

chosen_property.label: hasMonetaryAmount
chosen_property.definition: A relation indicating that a price specification has a monetary amount.
chosen_property.justification: Existing 'price' properties do not accommodate MonetaryAmount as a range.

candidates.label: price
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount. Examples: An offer has a price of '19.99'. A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.

candidates.label: priceRange
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the general price range of a local business, often expressed symbolically. Also called cost level, affordability, price point. Examples: A restaurant has a price range of '$$'. A store has a price range of '$$$'. The cafe has a price range of '$'.

candidates.label: priceValidUntil
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the date after which an offered price is no longer valid or available. Also called offer expiry date, price expiration, valid until date. Examples: An offer has a price valid until '2023-12-31'. The discount price is valid until 'next month'. The special offer's price valid until is '2024-01-15'.

candidates.label: priceCurrency
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the currency in which a price or price component is expressed. Also called currency type, monetary unit, unit of exchange. Examples: An offer has a price currency of 'USD'. A product's price currency is 'EUR'. The ticket price currency is 'GBP'. Distinct from price, which is the numerical value.

candidates.label: priceType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute defining the specific type of a price, such as a list price, sale price, or manufacturer suggested retail price. Also called pricing category, cost classification, rate type. Examples: A unit price specification has a price type of 'ListPrice'. A price has a price type of 'SalePrice'. The product's price type is 'MSRP'.

candidates.label: purchasePriceLimit
candidates.comment: A purchase price limit relation between a financial incentive and the maximum price an item can have to qualify for the incentive. Also called maximum price, price cap, qualifying price. Examples: "A rebate offer has a purchase price limit of $500.", "A discount coupon has a purchase price limit of €100.", "A loyalty bonus has a purchase price limit of £250."

candidates.label: highPrice
candidates.comment: A high price relation between an aggregate offer and the highest price among its available offers. Also called maximum price, highest cost, top price. Examples: "An aggregate offer has a high price of $100.", "The offers have a high price of '99.99'.", "This collection of offers shows a high price."

candidates.label: priceSpecification
candidates.comment: A financial attribute linking a demand, offer, or trade action to one or more detailed price specifications, including unit price and charges. Also called pricing details, cost breakdown, fee structure. Examples: An offer has a price specification for its unit price. A demand includes a price specification for delivery charges. The trade action details its price specification.

candidates.label: priceComponentType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute identifying the specific type of a price component, such as a line item on an invoice. Also called component type, charge type, fee category. Examples: A unit price specification has a price component type of 'BasePrice'. A price component has a price component type of 'Tax'. A line item has a price component type of 'ShippingFee'.

candidates.label: priceComponent
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a compound price specification and its individual unit price components. Also called price breakdown, cost element, pricing detail. Examples: A compound price specification includes a price component for 'base rate'. The total price has a price component for 'tax'. The invoice lists a price component for 'shipping fee'.

instances: US -> US military strikes against Iran
Houthi militia -> Houthi attacks on oil tankers in Red Sea

chosen_property.label: attendee
chosen_property.justification: The 'attendee' property is used in reverse to indicate the conductor of the event.

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: sensoryUnit
candidates.comment: The neurological pathway or anatomical structure that transmits sensory information to the brain or spinal cord. Also called sensory pathway, afferent pathway, nerve input. Examples: `Optic Nerve` sensoryUnit `Retina`, `Auditory Nerve` sensoryUnit `Cochlea`, `Median Nerve` sensoryUnit `Skin of Hand`. Distinct from `motorUnit`, which transmits motor commands.

candidates.label: byArtist
candidates.comment: A performance relation between a music album or recording and the music group or person who performed it. Also called "performed by", "artist of", "featuring artist". Examples: "Album 'Thriller' byArtist Michael Jackson", "Recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' byArtist Queen". Distinct from composer, which is the person who wrote the music, whereas byArtist is the performer.

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.

candidates.label: tracks
candidates.comment: A tracks relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist tracks 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup tracks 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album tracks 'Track 3'". Distinct from track, which can also refer to an ItemList of music recordings.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

instances: Iran -> US military strikes against Iran

chosen_property.label: targetCountry
chosen_property.definition: A relation indicating that an event is targeted at a specific country.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links Country to Event for 'targets'.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: targetName
candidates.comment: A textual name of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node name", "educational standard name", "learning objective name". Examples: "The alignment object has targetName 'Algebra I'", "The educational framework node's targetName is 'Critical Thinking'", "This targetName identifies a specific skill."

candidates.label: targetUrl
candidates.comment: A URL identifying a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node URL", "educational standard URL", "learning objective URL". Examples: "The alignment object has targetUrl 'http://example.com/algebra-standard'", "The educational framework node's targetUrl points to its definition", "This targetUrl links to a specific competency."

candidates.label: targetPlatform
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of platform for which an API reference is intended, such as phone or desktop. Also called "platform type", "development platform", "operating system target", "device target". Examples: "The API reference has targetPlatform iOS", "The software's targetPlatform is Windows Desktop", "This API is designed for targetPlatform Android."

candidates.label: targetProduct
candidates.comment: A compatibility relation between software source code and the software application or operating system it is intended for. Also called "compatible with", "designed for", "applies to product", "software target". Examples: "The source code has targetProduct Windows 10", "The script's targetProduct is Microsoft Excel", "This code is written for targetProduct Linux."

candidates.label: targetDescription
candidates.comment: A textual description of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node description", "educational standard description", "learning objective description". Examples: "The alignment object has targetDescription 'Understand basic algebra'", "The educational framework node's targetDescription explains the competency", "This targetDescription details a specific learning outcome."

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: targetPopulation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the characteristics of the intended or typical population for a dietary supplement or dose schedule. Also called "intended users", "demographic target", "user group", "audience characteristics". Examples: "The supplement has targetPopulation 'adults'", "The dose schedule's targetPopulation is 'children aged 6-12'", "This product is designed for a targetPopulation of athletes."

candidates.label: permitAudience
candidates.comment: A targeting relation between a permit and the specific audience it is intended for. Also called target group, eligible recipients, intended users. Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. A student permit has a permit audience of 'University Students'.

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property is used in reverse to indicate the location of the event.

instances: Congress -> Kevin Warsh states Fed has "no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation"

chosen_property.label: originatedAt
chosen_property.definition: A relation indicating that an inflation policy originates from an organization.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property links Organization to InflationPolicy for 'location'.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: workLocation
candidates.comment: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.

candidates.label: globalLocationNumber
candidates.comment: A global location number relation between an organization, person, or place and its unique 13-digit GLN identifier. Also called: GLN, International Location Number, ILN. Examples: "Acme Corp Warehouse" global location number "1234567890123", "Hospital Main Campus" global location number "9876543210987", "Distribution Center X" global location number "1122334455667".

instances: Strait of Hormuz -> Houthi attacks on oil tankers in Red Sea

chosen_property.label: threatensEvent
chosen_property.definition: A relation indicating that a defined region is a threat to an event.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property captures the threat from a region to an event.

candidates.label: risks
candidates.comment: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard
candidates.comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: estimatesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".

chosen_property.label: events
chosen_property.justification: The 'events' property allows a country (as a Place) to list events it experiences.

candidates.label: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
candidates.comment: An experience in place of education relation indicating whether a job posting accepts relevant experience as an alternative to formal educational qualifications. Also called: experience substitutes education, education equivalency, alternative qualification. Examples: "Senior Developer Job" experience in place of education "true", "Entry-Level Marketing Position" experience in place of education "false", "Project Manager Role" experience in place of education "true".

candidates.label: experienceRequirements
candidates.comment: An experience requirements relation between a job posting or occupation and the necessary skills and experience for the role. Also called: required experience, skill requirements, professional background. Examples: "Software Engineer Job" experience requirements "5+ years in Java development", "Marketing Manager Occupation" experience requirements "Proven track record in digital marketing campaigns", "Chef Position" experience requirements "Culinary school degree and 3 years restaurant experience".

candidates.label: monthsOfExperience
candidates.comment: A required number of months of experience for an occupational role. Also called experience duration, minimum experience, required experience in months. Examples: "Software Engineer Role monthsOfExperience 24", "Marketing Manager Position monthsOfExperience 60", "Entry-level Job monthsOfExperience 0".

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: photos
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to multiple photographs depicting it. Also called images, pictures, visual representations, gallery. Examples: A hotel has photos of its rooms and amenities. A museum has photos of its exhibits. A city has photos of its various attractions. Distinct from photo, which links to a single photograph.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

chosen_property.label: source
chosen_property.justification: The 'source' property is used in reverse to indicate the person as the source of the claim.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: costOrigin
candidates.comment: A source relation between a drug cost and additional details about where the cost data originated. Also called: cost data source, price origin, expense source. Examples: "Drug X cost" cost origin "Medicare Part B", "Medication Y price" cost origin "Private Insurance", "Prescription Z expense" cost origin "Manufacturer's List Price".

candidates.label: evidenceOrigin
candidates.comment: An evidence origin relation between a medical guideline and the source of data used to formulate it. Also called: data source, guideline source, origin of evidence. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" evidence origin "RCT", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" evidence origin "Consensus Opinion", "WHO Guideline for COVID-19" evidence origin "Observational Studies". Distinct from evidenceLevel, which is the strength of the evidence.

candidates.label: isBasedOnUrl
candidates.comment: A source URL relation between a creative work and a specific URL that served as a resource for its creation. Also called source URL, derived from URL, based on URL, reference URL. Examples: A research paper has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://arxiv.org/abs/1234.5678'. A blog post has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://example.com/original-article'. A web page has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://old-version.com/page'. Distinct from isBasedOn, which can refer to any CreativeWork or Product, not just a URL.

candidates.label: sourceOrganization
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a creative work and the organization on whose behalf its creator was working. Also called "commissioning organization", "producing organization", "organization behind", "publisher organization". Examples: "The research paper's sourceOrganization was MIT", "The documentary's sourceOrganization was BBC", "This report's sourceOrganization is the World Health Organization."

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: codeRepository
candidates.comment: A location relation for software source code, providing a URL to its repository. Also called "source code URL", "repository link", "code host". Examples: "Software project codeRepository 'https://github.com/example/project'", "Library source code codeRepository 'https://svn.example.org/repo'".

candidates.label: citation
candidates.comment: A reference relation between a creative work and another creative work or text that it cites. Also called "reference", "cited work", "source". Examples: "Research paper citation 'Smith, J. (2020). Article Title.'", "Blog post citation 'https://example.com/article'".

candidates.label: originalMediaLink
candidates.comment: A link to the original version of media content, such as a web page or a direct media object file, in a media review. Also called source media link, original content URL, primary media source. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaLink 'https://originalsource.com/video123'", "Image Review B originalMediaLink 'https://archive.org/image456'", "Audio Review C originalMediaLink 'https://podcast.example.com/episode789'". Distinct from url, which is the URL of the review itself.

chosen_property.label: affiliation
chosen_property.justification: The 'affiliation' property is used in reverse to indicate the organization's affiliation with the person.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: practicesAt
candidates.comment: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: subOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a parent organization and a smaller organization that is a part of it, such as a subsidiary. Also called "subsidiary", "division", "affiliated organization", "part of organization". Examples: "Google has subOrganization YouTube", "The university's subOrganization is the Computer Science Department", "This company owns several subOrganization entities.". Distinct from department, which is a more specific type of sub-organization.

candidates.label: colleagues
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and other persons who are their colleagues. Also called "co-workers", "associates", "professional peers". Examples: "John colleagues [Jane, Peter]", "Mary colleagues [Sarah, Tom]". Distinct from colleague, which is a singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

chosen_property.label: setsInterestRate
chosen_property.definition: A relation indicating that an organization sets a specific interest rate.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property links Organization to MonetaryAmount for 'sets'.

candidates.label: inDefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A defined term set inclusion relation between a defined term and the defined term set it belongs to. Also called part of term set, contained in term set, term set member. Examples: "A defined term is in a defined term set for medical conditions.", "The term is in a defined term set URL.", "This defined term belongs to a specific term set.". Distinct from hasDefinedTerm, which describes the inverse (set has term).

candidates.label: inCodeSet
candidates.comment: A code set inclusion relation between a category code and the category code set it belongs to. Also called part of code set, contained in code set, code set member. Examples: "A category code is in a code set for product types.", "The code is in a code set URL.", "This category code belongs to a specific code set.". Distinct from hasCategoryCode, which describes the inverse (set has code).

candidates.label: hasCategoryCode
candidates.comment: A code inclusion relation between a category code set and one of its contained category codes. Also called contains code, includes code, code within. Examples: "A product category set has a category code for electronics.", "A medical code set has a category code for diseases.", "The classification system has a category code for services."

candidates.label: repetitions
candidates.comment: A repetitions relation between an exercise plan and the number of times an activity should be performed. Also called number of reps, rep count. Examples: "An exercise plan specifies repetitions '10' for push-ups.", "A weightlifting routine includes repetitions '3 sets of 8'.", "A cardio workout has repetitions '30 minutes'."

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: steps
candidates.comment: A collection of individual instructions, sections, or creative works that constitute the steps of a how-to guide or section. Also called "how-to instructions", "procedure steps", "guide sections", "process stages". Examples: "The recipe has steps an ItemList of instructions", "The manual's steps include text and diagrams", "This how-to section outlines several steps.". Distinct from step, which refers to a single instruction or component.

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.

candidates.label: seasons
candidates.comment: A collection of seasons that constitute a radio, TV, or video game series. Also called series seasons, show seasons, installments. Examples: `TV Series: Game of Thrones` seasons `[Season 1, Season 2, ...]`, `Video Game Series: Call of Duty` seasons `[Modern Warfare Season, Cold War Season]`, `Radio Drama` seasons `[Season A, Season B]`. Distinct from `season`, which typically refers to a single season.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

chosen_property.label: exertsPressureOn

chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property captures this specific relation.

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: torque
candidates.comment: A torque relation between an engine specification and the turning force of the vehicle's engine. Also called engine torque, turning force, rotational force. Examples: "EngineSpecification torque '300 Nm'", "EngineSpecification torque '221 lb-ft'", "Vehicle engine torque '400 Nm'".

candidates.label: maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A physical attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can physically attend. Also called: in-person capacity, venue limit, on-site capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 500", "Live Concert maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 10000", "Workshop maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 30". Distinct from maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity, which refers to online attendees.

candidates.label: roofLoad
candidates.comment: The maximum permissible weight that can be carried on the roof of a vehicle, including cargo and any installations. Also called roof capacity, maximum roof weight, roof rack load limit. Examples: `SUV Model X` roofLoad `75 kg`, `Sedan Model Y` roofLoad `50 kg`, `Van Model Z` roofLoad `100 kg`. Distinct from `cargoVolume`, which refers to the internal cargo space.

candidates.label: engineDisplacement
candidates.comment: An engine displacement relation between an engine specification and the quantitative value representing the volume swept by all of the pistons inside the cylinders. Also called "engine volume", "cylinder capacity", "swept volume". Examples: "Engine specification engineDisplacement '2.0 LTR'", "Car engine engineDisplacement '1998 CMQ'", "Motorcycle engine engineDisplacement '750 INQ'".

candidates.label: cargoVolume
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement of the available volume for cargo or luggage in a vehicle. Also called "trunk volume", "luggage capacity", "storage volume". Examples: "Car vehicle cargoVolume 400 LTR", "Truck vehicle cargoVolume 100 FTQ".

candidates.label: antagonist
candidates.comment: An antagonist relation between a muscle and another muscle whose action opposes it. Also called opposing muscle, counteracting muscle. Examples: "The biceps' antagonist is the 'triceps'.", "The quadriceps' antagonist is the 'hamstrings'."

candidates.label: weightTotal
candidates.comment: A total weight capacity relation between a vehicle and a quantitative value, representing the maximum permitted loaded weight. Also called maximum weight, gross vehicle weight, total loaded weight, permitted weight. Examples: Truck weightTotal 40000 kg, Car weightTotal 2000 kg, Van weightTotal 3500 kg.

candidates.label: weightPercentage
candidates.comment: A fractional weight contribution relation between shipping rate settings and a numerical value, indicating the proportion of weight used for price calculation. Also called weight fraction, weight ratio, weight factor, weight proportion. Examples: ShippingRateSettings weightPercentage 0.10, ShippingRateSettings weightPercentage 0.05, ShippingRateSettings weightPercentage 0.25.

candidates.label: physicalRequirement
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the physical activities or abilities required for a job posting. Also called physical demands, fitness requirements, job physicality. Examples: A job posting has a physical requirement of 'ability to lift 50 lbs'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'standing for long periods'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'manual dexterity'.

chosen_property.label: predecessorOf
chosen_property.justification: The 'predecessorOf' property is used in reverse to indicate the predecessor relation between persons.

candidates.label: predecessorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a product model and its newer, often superseding, variant. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, updated to, newer version is. Examples: iPhone 10 is a predecessor of iPhone 11. Model A is a predecessor of Model B. The old software version is a predecessor of the new one. Distinct from successorOf, which points from a newer variant to an older one.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: founders
candidates.comment: A founders relation between an organization and the people who established it. Also called: co-founders, creators, originators. Examples: "Google" founders "Larry Page, Sergey Brin", "Apple Inc." founders "Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, Ronald Wayne", "Microsoft" founders "Bill Gates, Paul Allen". Distinct from founder, which can be a single person or organization.

candidates.label: foundingDate
candidates.comment: A founding date relation between an organization and the specific date it was established. Also called: establishment date, creation date, inception date. Examples: "Microsoft" founding date "1975-04-04", "Apple Inc." founding date "1976-04-01", "Google" founding date "1998-09-04".

candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners
candidates.comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: error

candidates.label: event

candidates.label: sportsEvent

candidates.label: actionStatus

candidates.label: actionProcess

candidates.label: eventStatus

candidates.label: events

Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". chosen_property.label: hasPreviousPrice

candidates.label: priceValidUntil

candidates.label: price

A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: priceRange
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the general price range of a local business, often expressed symbolically. Also called cost level, affordability, price point. Examples: A restaurant has a price range of '$$'. A store has a price range of '$$$'. The cafe has a price range of '$'.

candidates.label: highPrice
candidates.comment: A high price relation between an aggregate offer and the highest price among its available offers. Also called maximum price, highest cost, top price. Examples: "An aggregate offer has a high price of $100.", "The offers have a high price of '99.99'.", "This collection of offers shows a high price."

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: purchasePriceLimit
candidates.comment: A purchase price limit relation between a financial incentive and the maximum price an item can have to qualify for the incentive. Also called maximum price, price cap, qualifying price. Examples: "A rebate offer has a purchase price limit of $500.", "A discount coupon has a purchase price limit of €100.", "A loyalty bonus has a purchase price limit of £250."

candidates.label: priceType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute defining the specific type of a price, such as a list price, sale price, or manufacturer suggested retail price. Also called pricing category, cost classification, rate type. Examples: A unit price specification has a price type of 'ListPrice'. A price has a price type of 'SalePrice'. The product's price type is 'MSRP'.

candidates.label: priceCurrency
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the currency in which a price or price component is expressed. Also called currency type, monetary unit, unit of exchange. Examples: An offer has a price currency of 'USD'. A product's price currency is 'EUR'. The ticket price currency is 'GBP'. Distinct from price, which is the numerical value.

candidates.label: lowPrice
candidates.comment: A lowest price relation between an aggregate offer and the lowest price among all available offers. Also called: minimum price, cheapest price, starting price. Examples: "Product Bundle lowPrice 9.99", "Flight Deals lowPrice 150.00", "Software License lowPrice 49.99". Distinct from minPrice, which is the lowest price in a range for a single price specification.
